images.filename: Lowland (Cornish) Heath at Goonhilly Downs - geograph.org.uk - 712919.jpg
images.caption: Lowland (Cornish) Heath at Goonhilly Downs View northwards from the lane to the Satellite Earth Station. Parts of this land have SSSI status and contain some of the rarest heathland plants in the UK. The down as a whole is Open Access, but plant preservation is helped by restricted access to the various BT sites. Parts of the land are also grazed by ponies under licence.

images.caption:
One of the fastest Internet connections in Britain (and they were watching youtube)

One thing I'll take from Goonhilly is that communications started digitally in data with morse code, then went voice, then data (the Internet) was sent along the voice infrasturucture, now the voice infrastructure is being replaced by a data one carrying voice! It was amazing also to learn how Goonhilly plays a role in International communications.

images.caption: Panoramic view of the geodesic dome structures of the Eden Project. The Eden Project is a large-scale environmental complex near St Austell, Cornwall, England, United Kingdom. The project was conceived by Tim Smit and has quickly become one of the most popular visitor attractions in the United Kingdom. The complex includes two giant, translucent domes made of ETFE cushions, each emulating a natural biome, that house plant species from around the world. The first emulates a tropical environment, the other a warm temperate, mediterranean environment. The project took 2½ years to construct and opened to the public in March 2001.
